Subject: Dedicated capacity baseline + draft SLA options

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for the discussion today — good to see the Brightline team thinking through predictable production economics. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the Dedicated capacity options we discussed and flag two things we know procurement will care about: (1) how throughput guarantees will be measured (tokens/sec and requests/sec), and (2) how latency targets map to those guarantees.

High-level options (we can iterate on numbers):
- Option A (Standard commit): 3x A100-equivalent GPU pool, baseline 120k tokens/sec sustained, 80 req/sec (avg seq 256), 95th pct latency target = 250 ms.
- Option B (Enterprise commit): 6x A100-equivalent GPU pool, baseline 300k tokens/sec sustained, 200 req/sec, 95th pct latency target = 180 ms, and 99th pct fallback tier.

We can offer a stepped discount on committed monthly spend: 10% at 6-month commit, 18% at 12-month, 25% at 24-month with a minimum commit level.

You mentioned procurement wants a formal measurement protocol and clear acceptance criteria. Vivek and Aditya are looped in to propose a concise, reproducible test plan (including warm-up, model selection, seq-length distribution, and how we count tokens). I’ll also attach the draft protocol and pricing spreadsheet for reference.

Next step: if you can confirm the model family (e.g., Llama 2 70B or an equivalent), and a rough distribution of sequence lengths (p95 token count), we’ll tailor the test harness and firm up numbers.

Thanks —
Monica

Monica,

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifying questions from procurement/infra:

1) Measurement scope — we need a clear definition of tokens/sec: is that aggregate across the whole GPU pool or per-GPU and then summed? Also, do you count user prompt tokens + generated tokens or only generated?

2) Latency SLOs — procurement prefers P95 and P99 numbers with the exact request size/profile used during measurement.

3) Test conditions — please confirm whether the tests are run on a representative model (we plan to use Llama 2 70B q4 or equivalent) and whether the harness will include mixed batch sizes and a realistic seq-length distribution (p50=128, p90=512, p99=2048 approx for our workload).

4) Measurement repeatability — we need a documented protocol we can run ourselves (or agree to run jointly). If you provide a harness and configs we can run in our environment, that would speed acceptance.

5) Pricing detail — the discount schedule is fine in principle; procurement also wants the SLA credit policy if you miss tokens/sec or latency targets.

Can Vivek/Vivek's team provide the formal protocol and a sample SLA credit calculation so procurement can review?

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity baseline + draft SLA options — measurement protocol + sample credits

Hi Daniel, Monica — appreciate the clear list. Attached is a consolidated protocol and two sample artifacts: pricing spreadsheet and the test harness config. Key points below (TL;DR first):

TL;DR- Tokens/sec = aggregate sum of tokens produced + tokens consumed (i.e., prompt + response) across all GPUs in the dedicated pool, measured as an average over a sustained 10-minute window after warm-up.
- Requests/sec is counted as completed request transactions per second (end-to-end), using success criteria (HTTP 200 + response validation).
- Latency SLOs are expressed as P95 and P99 on end-to-end request latency measured at the ingress load generator.
- Measurement harness: we provide a Dockerized load generator (test-harness-config.yaml attached) that runs realistic mixes (batch sizes 1–8, sequence length distribution: p50=128, p90=512, p99=2048 by default).

Detailed protocol (summary):
1) Environment: tests run against the Dedicated GPU pool configured for the customer. We can run jointly (Redwood-managed test run) or provide the harness for Brightline to run in their staging.
2) Model: test on Llama2-70B q4 (or equivalent) — quantization and model binary must be identical between runs to compare results.
3) Warm-up: 5–10 minute warm-up with progressively increasing QPS to prime KV caches and compilation kernels. Warm-up traffic is excluded from measurement.
4) Measurement window: 10-minute sustained run; we take the average tokens/sec over the central 8 minutes (drop first and last minute) to avoid edge artifacts. Simultaneously record per-request latencies; compute P50/P95/P99.
5) Token counting: we count prompt tokens + generated tokens using the same tokenizer (BPE) version; token counts are aggregated across the pool and reported as tokens/sec.
6) Mixes: a set of load profiles (interactive low-latency, batch high-throughput, mixed) are included. The SLA will specify which profile is authoritative for a given commit (typically "mixed" unless otherwise agreed).
7) Failure handling: if any GPU node reports hardware errors or OOMs, that run is marked invalid and may be re-run once the cluster is healthy.
8) Acceptance criteria & credits:
   - If measured tokens/sec falls below the committed baseline by >5% for two consecutive weekly measurements, customer is eligible for credits.
   - Latency miss: if P95 exceeds target for a billing window more than 3 days in a month, credit = X% of monthly committed fee (sample calculations in attached spreadsheet).

Sample numbers (from a mocked run):
- 6x A100-equivalent pool -> observed steady-state: 315k tokens/sec aggregate, 210 req/sec (mixed profile), P95 latency = 165 ms.
- Using the pricing spreadsheet: 12-month commit at that capacity yields an estimated 18% discount vs pay-as-you-go; SLA credit policy caps at 30% of monthly committed fee in extreme cases.

Attachments included: SLA-measurement-protocol-v1.pdf (formal text), pricing-options-commits.xlsx (sample pricing + credit calc), test-harness-config.yaml (example load profile).

If Brightline prefers, we can run the test jointly next Tuesday and share a live dashboard during the run. If you want the harness to run internally, Aditya — please paste the minimal run commands and any credentials required below.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek, Monica — this looks good and answers procurement's primary concerns. A couple of small asks before we proceed to legal/DocuSign:

1) Please add an explicit definition of "sustained window" in the protocol (you used 10-minute window and drop first/last minute — please include a short rationale).
2) For the credit calc, include a worked example where P95 target = 180 ms and measured P95 = 210 ms for one billing week so procurement can see the dollar impact.

If you include those two items we can route to legal and hit signatures next week. Procurement contact (cc'd) is ready to receive the DocuSign package — please share estimated SLA start date (we anticipate onboarding in Sep 2026 if everything signs).

Thanks —
Daniel
